home.title: GarbellaVeus
home.p1Pre: Want to help us improve Catalan speech technology? Evaluate voice clips from the
home.p1Post: dataset, about 920 hours extracted from plenary session videos, with audio under the
home.p1PostLicense: license (free to reuse as long as credit is given). The transcriptions are automatic and not all of them are correct, and some clips aren't even in Catalan. With your evaluations we can separate the reliable material from the rest and publish an open dataset of human-validated Catalan speech.
home.p2: It's simple: listen to the clips and vote on whether the transcription and dialect are correct. If you spot errors, you can also contribute by suggesting a more accurate transcription or identifying the correct dialect.
home.p3Link: transcriptions automatically verified by the BSC
home.p3Post: , to now add a layer of human validation on top.

guidelines.title: What makes a good transcription
short: Transcribe literally what you hear: including Spanish-isms, grammatical mistakes and dialect forms (e.g. "eixes").
Don't add or omit words, and don't "improve" what the speaker said.
Use punctuation and capital letters (sentence starts, proper nouns).
Numbers can be written as digits (2015); abbreviations as they are pronounced.
guidelines.pageIntro: This guide explains what we look for in a good transcription and why. Listen to the audio carefully and read the text closely: every evaluation helps train Catalan speech recognition models.

rules.title: Be literal: write what is said, not what "should" be said
rules.text: The transcription must faithfully reflect speech, including Spanish-isms ("en quant a", "m'agradaria destacar una cosa") and grammatical mistakes. Don't correct them.
rules.why: This keeps as much information as possible. If something needs to be removed later it can be done automatically; adding it back would require someone to redo the work we are doing now.

examples.audio: en quant a l'aprovació del pressupost, doncs…
examples.wrong: Pel que fa a l'aprovació del pressupost, doncs…
examples.right: En quant a l'aprovació del pressupost, doncs…

rules.title: Dialect forms and vocabulary: respect the speaker's variety
rules.text: If the proposed text has "normalised" a word or grammatical form but the audio is clearly different, correct it.
rules.why: The dataset is used to train models that must understand every variety of Catalan. If transcriptions flatten dialects, models learn that everyone speaks the same way.

rules.title: Hesitations and interjections: include them
rules.text: Write "eh", "mmm", "bé", "a veure", repetitions and abandoned sentence starts as they are pronounced.
rules.why: They are part of real speech and recognition models must handle them. Stripping them from a text is trivial; adding them afterwards is not.

examples.audio: eh… a veure, jo crec que, que sí
examples.right: Eh… a veure, jo crec que, que sí.

rules.title: No more, no fewer words
rules.text: Don't add words that weren't said or leave out any that were, even if the sentence would read better or shorter.
rules.why: A transcription is only useful for training if text and audio match. An extra or missing word puts noise straight into the data.

examples.audio: avui parlarem del pressupost de l'any vinent
examples.right: Avui parlarem del pressupost de l'any vinent.

rules.title: Punctuation and capitals: yes, standard ones
rules.text: Use commas, periods, question and exclamation marks following intonation and meaning, and capitalise sentence starts and proper nouns.
rules.why: We deliberately apply no normalisation. Current models such as Whisper are trained with punctuation and capitalisation; keeping them leaves the door open for future decisions. Removing them is easy; adding them is not.

examples.audio: bon dia a tothom avui parlarem de l'ajuntament de girona
examples.wrong: bon dia a tothom avui parlarem de l'ajuntament de girona
examples.right: Bon dia a tothom. Avui parlarem de l'Ajuntament de Girona.

rules.title: Numbers and abbreviations
rules.text: Write numbers and dates as digits: there's no need to write "dos mil quinze" instead of "2015". Abbreviations, on the other hand, are written as pronounced (if the speaker says "senyor", don't write "Sr.").
rules.why: Converting digits to words can be done programmatically and reliably. The other direction is harder, and digits are more natural to read and write.

examples.audio: l'any dos mil quinze vam aprovar el pla

scoring: Each "Correct" vote adds one point and each "Incorrect" vote subtracts one.
Once a transcription reaches two points it is considered valid.
When someone corrects a transcription, the correction gets one point, but another person still has to mark it correct for it to be considered valid.
If two people submit a correction with exactly the same text, their points add up and count as a single validation.
No normalisation of the text (punctuation, capitals, numbers…) is applied, deliberately, to avoid losing information. We can always normalise and merge later if we see fit.
guidelines.imperfectText: If a word is hard to make out, do your best; if the clip is impossible to evaluate, you can skip it or report it.

about.title: About this project
about.datasetText: This platform hosts human evaluation of the Catalan YouTube Speech Corpus: 231,684 short clips of spontaneous Catalan speech, automatically extracted from public YouTube videos by Softcatalà, with audio under a CC-BY license and transcripts and metadata under MIT. Each clip includes an automatic transcription (some already filtered to higher confidence by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center) and, for some clips, a detected dialect; corrections and votes from the community are collected here.
about.licenseMid: license of the original YouTube videos: it can be freely copied, adapted and reused, even commercially, as long as the original videos are credited. The
about.licensePost: license allows the same for the transcripts and metadata.
about.whyText: The transcripts were produced automatically, not reviewed by a person, so the dataset is raw and unvalidated, useful for large-scale training, but not a reliable benchmark on its own. Where the two automatic candidates agree, the text is usually trustworthy; where they diverge, the clip is often noisy, overlapping speech, or otherwise hard to transcribe.
about.limitsText: Most clips come from municipal plenary sessions and other institutional events. The dataset therefore mostly reflects a formal register and the speech of adults with a political or institutional profile; colloquial speech, young voices and everyday topics are missing. Models trained on this data may perform worse on those other registers.
about.limitsCallText: We're looking for Catalan audio and video from other settings (informal conversation, radio and podcasts, schools, cultural events, young voices…) that can be freely reused, under permissive licenses such as CC-BY or CC0 or in the public domain, and with the consent of the people who appear in it. If you have some or know of any,
about.goalText: Every vote you cast, on a transcription or a detected dialect, helps build a human-validated layer on top of this raw automatic data: surfacing which transcriptions can be trusted, catching what the models got wrong, and producing higher-confidence data that can be used to improve Catalan speech recognition.
